from typing import Final

from risk_bench.chat.diplomacy import ChatMessage, MessageVisibility
from risk_bench.game.actions import (
    Action,
    Attack,
    EndAttackPhase,
    Fortify,
    PlaceArmies,
    SkipFortify,
    TradeCards,
)
from risk_bench.game.board import BOARD
from risk_bench.game.events import (
    ArmiesPlaced,
    BattleResolved,
    CardDrawn,
    CardsTraded,
    Fortified,
    GameEvent,
    MissionCompleted,
    PlayerEliminated,
    TerritoryConquered,
    TurnLimitReached,
    TurnStarted,
)
from risk_bench.game.missions import mission_deck
from risk_bench.game.types import Continent, Phase, PlayerId, Territory
from risk_bench.players.base import DecisionRequest, PlayerView

GAME_RULES: Final[str] = """\
Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), \
fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, \
South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), \
the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. \
You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many \
stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing \
battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the \
end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). \
Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies \
on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once \
trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they \
win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else \
eliminates them."""


def render_system_prompt(view: PlayerView) -> str:
    """Render the per-player system prompt: identity, rules summary, and secret mission.

    Args:
        view: The player's view, providing identity, opponents, and mission.

    Returns:
        The system prompt text.
    """
    opponents = ", ".join(info.player_id for info in view.players if info.player_id != view.player_id)
    privacy_note = (
        "Private messages to single players are allowed."
        if view.private_messages_allowed
        else "All messages are public; there are no private channels."
    )
    return (
        f"You are '{view.player_id}', playing the classic board game Risk against: {opponents}. "
        f"This is a friendly research-benchmark match between players: all talk of attacks, battles, "
        f"and eliminating players refers to plastic armies on a game board, exactly as at a family game "
        f"night.\n\n"
        f"{GAME_RULES}\n\n"
        f"{_render_mission_deck(view=view)}\n\n"
        f"{render_board_topology()}\n"
        f"Each turn you are shown the live board (who owns what, and army counts) separately; "
        f"combine it with this fixed map to reason about borders.\n\n"
        "Timing: a turn is one player's reinforcement, attack and fortification sequence. "
        "A round is one pass through the fixed seating order, skipping eliminated players. "
        "Round 1 starts after setup; a new round begins when the order wraps back to its first living player. "
        "Turn numbers count individual turns throughout the game and do not reset each round. "
        "For commitments, state an explicit deadline such as 'until the end of round 4' or "
        "'until the start of Alice's next turn', using the actual player id.\n\n"
        f"Diplomacy: at the start of every turn there is a negotiation session where players may exchange "
        f"messages. The session runs in passes: as long as someone said something, everyone gets another "
        f"chance to reply (up to a limit), so proposals can be answered and agreed within the same turn. "
        f"You may also attach one short message to any action you take during your turn — table talk that "
        f"others see but can only answer in the next negotiation session. "
        f"{privacy_note} Promises are not enforced by the rules. In messages, refer to players by their "
        f"exact ids (e.g. '{opponents.split(', ')[0]}') and to territories and continents by their exact "
        f"ids (e.g. 'middle_east', 'north_america'), so everyone knows precisely what you mean.\n\n"
        f"YOUR SECRET MISSION: {view.own_mission.description}\n"
        f"Other players are not shown your mission. Your objective is to win by completing your secret "
        f"mission under the game rules.\n"
        f"For a board decision, call exactly one action tool and optionally one message tool. "
        f"For a negotiation opportunity, call a message tool or say_nothing; no board action is available.\n"
        "Every game action and send_public_message call requires a private_memo string argument "
        "INSIDE its arguments: 1–1200 characters briefly stating what you intend and why. "
        "say_nothing and send_private_message need no memo. To stay silent, call say_nothing({}). "
        "Plain response text is optional and does not replace private_memo. "
        "This is a brief decision summary, not hidden reasoning. It is not shown to other players. "
        "The memo and all tool calls are validated before anything is executed or sent."
    )


def _render_mission_deck(view: PlayerView) -> str:
    # The deck is printed in the rules of the physical game: a player at a table knows which
    # missions exist and can reason about what an opponent's play implies. Withholding it would
    # make deduction about hidden goals — and any lie about one's own — unanchored.
    cards = mission_deck(player_ids=[info.player_id for info in view.players])
    listing = "\n".join(f"- {card.description}" for card in cards)
    return (
        f"The mission deck is public; only the deal is secret. It holds these {len(cards)} cards, "
        f"of which {len(view.players)} were dealt face down, one to each player:\n{listing}\n"
        f"You hold one of them and know which; the other {len(cards) - 1} are the pool every "
        f"opponent's card was dealt from. What a player attacks, defends and asks for is evidence "
        f"about which one they hold."
    )


def render_decision_prompt(request: DecisionRequest) -> str:
    """Render a decision point: notes, this turn's events and chat, board, standings, and the task.

    Only the current turn's events and chat are shown; everything older the player
    carries in its own notes. The board is serialized grouped by continent with
    owners and army counts, so the model never has to recall the map from memory.

    Args:
        request: The decision point to render.

    Returns:
        The user-turn prompt text for the decision.
    """
    view = request.view
    sections = [
        _render_timing(view),
        f"{view.phase} phase. It is your move.",
        _render_notes(view=view),
        _render_events(view=view),
        _render_chat(view=view),
        _render_additional_context(view=view),
        _render_players(view=view),
        _render_board(view=view),
        _render_hand(view=view),
        f"Reminder of your secret mission: {view.own_mission.description}",
        _phase_instruction(request=request),
        "You may optionally include ONE message tool call alongside your action tool call to address the "
        "other players; most actions need no message.",
    ]
    return "\n\n".join(section for section in sections if section)


def render_negotiation_prompt(view: PlayerView) -> str:
    """Render a negotiation opportunity: events, standings, board, and the visible chat.

    Args:
        view: The player's current view of the game.

    Returns:
        The user-turn prompt text inviting diplomacy messages.
    """
    speaker_note = (
        "It is your turn; you may open the negotiation session."
        if view.current_player == view.player_id
        else f"It is {view.current_player}'s turn; you may react."
    )
    sections = [
        _render_timing(view),
        f"Negotiation session. {speaker_note}",
        _render_notes(view=view),
        _render_events(view=view),
        _render_chat(view=view),
        _render_additional_context(view=view),
        _render_players(view=view),
        _render_board(view=view),
        f"Reminder of your secret mission: {view.own_mission.description}",
        "You may send a message or remain silent. Choose whichever best serves your game strategy.",
    ]
    return "\n\n".join(section for section in sections if section)


def render_noting_prompt(view: PlayerView) -> str:
    """Render the end-of-turn noting prompt: the turn just played, then a rewrite instruction.

    A dedicated, neutral call: the model rereads the turn that just ended and its
    own previous notes, then rewrites a fresh, bounded notepad. These notes are
    the only memory it keeps of earlier turns, so what it records, consolidates,
    or drops is entirely its own choice.

    Args:
        view: The noting player's view, carrying the just-ended turn's events and
            chat plus the player's current notes.

    Returns:
        The user-turn prompt text inviting a notes rewrite.
    """
    sections = [
        f"Round {view.previous_round_number} · Turn {view.turn_number - 1} just ended. "
        "Update the private notes you keep for your "
        "future self before the next turn proceeds.",
        "Current board: " + _render_timing(view),
        _render_events(view=view),
        _render_chat(view=view),
        _render_additional_context(view=view),
        _render_players(view=view),
        _render_board(view=view),
        _render_notes_for_update(view=view),
        _NOTING_INSTRUCTION,
    ]
    return "\n\n".join(section for section in sections if section)


def _render_timing(view: PlayerView) -> str:
    position = (
        "Setup placement, before round 1."
        if view.turn_number == 0
        else f"Round {view.round_number} · Turn {view.turn_number} · {view.current_player}'s turn."
    )
    order = " → ".join(player.player_id for player in view.players if not player.is_eliminated)
    return f"{position}\nTurn order (living players): {order}."


# soft target the noting prompt suggests, so a long game's notes stay bounded; not enforced
_NOTES_WORD_BUDGET: Final[int] = 200

_NOTING_INSTRUCTION: Final[str] = (
    "These notes are your only memory of earlier turns: on your next turn the live board and the "
    "fixed map are always shown again, so you never need to record who owns what or how many armies "
    "sit where — only what the board cannot tell you later (intentions, promises, threats, alliances, "
    "who did what to whom, and your own plans). Rewrite your notes from scratch: keep what still "
    "matters, drop what has gone stale, and fold in anything you learned this turn. Keep them concise "
    f"(aim for under about {_NOTES_WORD_BUDGET} words). Reply with the notes themselves as plain text "
    "and nothing else."
)


# An experimental intervention is rendered as information the player has, in the same register as
# the rest of the game context: framing it as an instruction, or as the player's own recollection,
# would change what a comparison between two forks actually measures.
def _render_additional_context(view: PlayerView) -> str:
    if not view.additional_context:
        return ""
    return f"Additional information available to you:\n{view.additional_context}"


def _render_notes(view: PlayerView) -> str:
    if not view.notes:
        return ""
    return f"Your private notes (your memory of earlier turns; only you can see them):\n{view.notes}"


def _render_notes_for_update(view: PlayerView) -> str:
    if not view.notes:
        return "Your notes so far: (none yet — this is your first set.)"
    return f"Your notes so far:\n{view.notes}"


def _render_events(view: PlayerView) -> str:
    if not view.recent_events:
        return ""
    lines = "\n".join(f"- {narrate_event(event=event)}" for event in view.recent_events)
    return f"This turn so far:\n{lines}"


def _render_chat(view: PlayerView) -> str:
    if not view.visible_chat:
        return ""
    lines = "\n".join(f"- {_format_message(message=message)}" for message in view.visible_chat)
    return f"Messages this turn (most recent last):\n{lines}"


def _format_message(message: ChatMessage) -> str:
    channel = "to everyone" if message.visibility is MessageVisibility.PUBLIC else f"privately to {message.recipient}"
    return f"turn {message.turn_number}, {message.sender} {channel}: {message.text}"


def _render_players(view: PlayerView) -> str:
    lines = []
    for info in view.players:
        if info.is_eliminated:
            lines.append(f"- {info.player_id}: ELIMINATED")
        else:
            lines.append(
                f"- {info.player_id}: {info.territory_count} territories, {info.army_count} armies, "
                f"{info.card_count} cards, income {info.income}/turn"
            )
    return "Players:\n" + "\n".join(lines)


def render_board_text(owner: dict[Territory, PlayerId], armies: dict[Territory, int]) -> str:
    """Serialize the board grouped by continent with owners, army counts, and adjacency.

    Args:
        owner: The owning player of every territory.
        armies: The army count on every territory.

    Returns:
        The board as prompt text; used by the commentator, which sees one
        self-contained omniscient view per turn rather than a cached prefix.
    """
    lines = []
    for continent in Continent:
        continent_info = BOARD.continent_info(continent)
        lines.append(f"{continent} (+{continent_info.army_bonus} bonus for owning all of it):")
        for territory in sorted(continent_info.territories):
            neighbors = ", ".join(sorted(BOARD.neighbors_of(territory)))
            lines.append(f"  {territory}: {owner[territory]} with {armies[territory]} armies | borders: {neighbors}")
    return "Board:\n" + "\n".join(lines)


def render_board_topology() -> str:
    """Serialize the fixed map: continents, their bonuses, and each territory's borders.

    The topology never changes during a game, so it is sent once in the system
    prompt (and cached there) instead of being re-sent with every decision.

    Returns:
        The static map as prompt text.
    """
    lines = []
    for continent in Continent:
        continent_info = BOARD.continent_info(continent)
        lines.append(f"{continent} (+{continent_info.army_bonus} bonus for owning all of it):")
        for territory in sorted(continent_info.territories):
            neighbors = ", ".join(sorted(BOARD.neighbors_of(territory)))
            lines.append(f"  {territory} borders: {neighbors}")
    return "The map is fixed for the whole game. Territories by continent, with the bonus and borders:\n" + "\n".join(
        lines
    )


def render_board_state(owner: dict[Territory, PlayerId], armies: dict[Territory, int]) -> str:
    """Serialize the live board: who owns each territory and how many armies sit on it.

    Adjacency is omitted because it is fixed and already given by the map in the
    system prompt; only the changing ownership and army counts are sent each turn.

    Args:
        owner: The owning player of every territory.
        armies: The army count on every territory.

    Returns:
        The current board state as prompt text.
    """
    lines = []
    for continent in Continent:
        continent_info = BOARD.continent_info(continent)
        lines.append(f"{continent}:")
        for territory in sorted(continent_info.territories):
            lines.append(f"  {territory}: {owner[territory]} with {armies[territory]} armies")
    return "Current board (owner and armies per territory):\n" + "\n".join(lines)


def _render_board(view: PlayerView) -> str:
    return render_board_state(owner=view.owner, armies=view.armies)


def _render_hand(view: PlayerView) -> str:
    if not view.own_cards:
        return "Your cards: none."
    labels = ", ".join(
        "wild" if card.territory is None else f"{card.design}({card.territory})" for card in view.own_cards
    )
    return f"Your cards: {labels}"


def _phase_instruction(request: DecisionRequest) -> str:
    view = request.view
    match view.phase:
        case Phase.SETUP_PLACEMENT:
            return (
                f"Setup: place your starting armies ({view.armies_to_place} left); you can split them across "
                f"territories in one call. Other players' placements are hidden until the game begins, and "
                f"yours are hidden from them."
            )
        case Phase.REINFORCE:
            return (
                f"Reinforce: you have {view.armies_to_place} armies to place, splittable across territories "
                f"in one call. Trade cards first if you wish."
            )
        case Phase.ATTACK:
            if any(isinstance(action, TradeCards) for action in request.legal_actions):
                return (
                    f"Attack phase, but you now hold {len(view.own_cards)} cards after taking an eliminated "
                    f"player's hand: you must trade in a set before you can attack again."
                )
            if any(isinstance(action, PlaceArmies) for action in request.legal_actions):
                return (
                    f"Attack phase: place the {view.armies_to_place} armies from your forced card trade on your "
                    f"territories (splittable across territories in one call), then you can continue attacking."
                )
            return (
                "Attack: launch one or more attacks on adjacent enemy territories (you can repeat against a "
                "target until it falls), or end the attack phase."
            )
        case Phase.FORTIFY:
            return "Fortify: optionally move armies between two adjacent territories you own; this ends your turn."
        case Phase.GAME_OVER:
            return "The game is over."


def narrate_event(event: GameEvent) -> str:
    """Render one game event as a human-readable sentence.

    Args:
        event: The event to narrate.

    Returns:
        A single-sentence description, used in prompts and the replay viewer.
    """
    match event:
        case TurnStarted(player_id=player_id, turn_number=turn_number):
            return f"Turn {turn_number} started for {player_id}."
        case ArmiesPlaced(player_id=player_id, territory=territory, count=count):
            return f"{player_id} placed {count} armies on {territory}."
        case CardsTraded(player_id=player_id, card_designs=designs, bonus_armies=bonus):
            return f"{player_id} traded a card set ({', '.join(designs)}) for {bonus} armies."
        case BattleResolved(attacker=attacker, defender=defender, outcome=outcome) as battle:
            return (
                f"{attacker} attacked {battle.to_territory} from {battle.from_territory}: "
                f"rolled {list(outcome.attacker_dice)} vs {defender}'s {list(outcome.defender_dice)} — "
                f"attacker lost {outcome.attacker_losses}, defender lost {outcome.defender_losses}."
            )
        case TerritoryConquered(player_id=player_id, territory=territory, from_territory=from_territory):
            return f"{player_id} conquered {territory} from {from_territory}."
        case Fortified(player_id=player_id, from_territory=from_territory, to_territory=to_territory, count=count):
            return f"{player_id} fortified, moving {count} armies from {from_territory} to {to_territory}."
        case CardDrawn(player_id=player_id):
            return f"{player_id} earned a territory card."
        case PlayerEliminated(eliminated_player=eliminated_player, eliminated_by=eliminated_by):
            return f"{eliminated_player} was ELIMINATED by {eliminated_by}, who takes their cards."
        case MissionCompleted(player_id=player_id, mission_description=description):
            return f"{player_id} WON the game by completing their mission: {description}"
        case TurnLimitReached(turn_number=turn_number):
            return f"The game hit the turn limit at turn {turn_number} and ends in a draw."


def describe_action(player_id: PlayerId, action: Action) -> str:
    """Render one applied action as a short present-tense sentence.

    Used by the replay viewer and the evaluator's trace index, so a citation and
    a replay step describe the same move identically.

    Args:
        player_id: The player who took the action.
        action: The action to describe.

    Returns:
        A single-sentence description of the action.
    """
    match action:
        case PlaceArmies(territory=territory, count=count):
            return f"{player_id} places {count} armies on {territory}"
        case TradeCards(cards=cards):
            labels = ", ".join(
                "wild" if card.territory is None else f"{card.design}({card.territory})" for card in cards
            )
            return f"{player_id} trades in {labels}"
        case Attack(
            from_territory=from_territory, to_territory=to_territory, attacker_dice=dice, max_attacks=max_attacks
        ):
            repeat = f" up to {max_attacks} times" if max_attacks > 1 else ""
            return f"{player_id} attacks {to_territory} from {from_territory} with {dice} dice{repeat}"
        case Fortify(from_territory=from_territory, to_territory=to_territory, count=count):
            return f"{player_id} fortifies {count} armies from {from_territory} to {to_territory}"
        case EndAttackPhase():
            return f"{player_id} ends the attack phase"
        case SkipFortify():
            return f"{player_id} ends the turn without fortifying"

changes.pending:
My mission: Europe + South America + a third continent. Oceania (via siam–indonesia) or Africa (via north_africa) are the candidates.

PACTS:
- claude–gemini: no attacks between us until the end of round 3, reconfirmed in turn 3.
  - Don't break it early; reputation matters.
  - Strike iceland, northern_europe and scandinavia right after it ends.
  - Build up in western_europe, great_britain and ukraine for that.
- claude–gpt (agreed turn 4): neither attacks the other across siam–indonesia until the end of round 3, whoever owns them. Nothing else is covered.
  - north_africa and all other borders stay open.
  - I may still attack gpt elsewhere, e.g. mongolia/siberia, or Oceania via another route; there is none except siam.

gpt:
- Took indonesia from gemini in turn 4 and owns all of Oceania now, with 4 armies on indonesia.
- Likely mission involves Oceania (NA+Oceania? Europe+Oceania?). It also holds most of NA thinly.
- Wanted a truce covering north_africa, so it values north_africa; probably fears me there.

gemini:
- Holds Africa except north_africa.
- Likely Asia+Africa or NA+Africa.
- Main rival for Africa.

Plan:
- Take north_africa from gpt (2 armies) with a stack from brazil. This blocks gemini's Africa and opens Africa as my third continent.
- After round 3: take gemini's Europe; Oceania via siam is also available then.
- Guard venezuela, southern_europe.
- Asia is expendable.
- Keep my mission hidden; frame gpt as the common target.

$map:
Mission: Conquer 24 territories (self-elimination fallback). Keep secret.

Commitments: claude-opus-5-5 and gemini-3.8-flash reaffirmed mutual non-aggression through the end of round 3. My pact with claude-opus-5-5 prohibits attacks across siam–indonesia through the end of round 3, even if ownership changes. No other borders protected. gemini-3.8-flash rejected my proposed full-border NAP but stated no designs on my asia or oceania holdings; this is an intention, not an agreement.

History: claude-opus-5-5 took my South American/European holdings, completed south_america, and captured my north_africa on turn 5. I completed oceania on turn 4. On turn 6, gemini-3.8-flash reinforced western_united_states and captured my ontario without losses.

Diplomacy: claude-opus-5-5 actively encourages gemini-3.8-flash to take my north_america holdings. I highlighted claude-opus-5-5’s army/income lead and suggested negotiating north_africa for gemini-3.8-flash’s africa bonus; no acceptance.

Mission clues: claude-opus-5-5 may seek europe/south_america/third continent. gemini-3.8-flash explicitly prioritizes north_america, potentially consistent with north_america/africa. Neither inference is firm.

Plan: Preserve oceania income, concentrate rather than scatter reinforcements, and seek affordable expansion toward 24. Consider thin asia targets accessible from mongolia/siberia while honoring siam–indonesia. Expect coordinated pressure through round 3; seek to divide opponents before their pact expires.

My mission: Europe + South America + a third continent. South America is held. Third continent: Africa (via north_africa) or Oceania (via siam).

PACTS:
- claude–gemini: no attacks between us until the end of round 3, confirmed again in turn 6. Honor it.
  - From round 4, strike iceland, northern_europe and scandinavia (thin), then gemini's Africa.
  - Mass in western_europe, great_britain, ukraine and north_africa before round 4.
- claude–gpt (turn 4): no attacks across siam–indonesia until the end of round 3. Nothing else is covered.

gpt:
- Weakest player (15 armies). Holds Oceania plus thin NA singles and mongolia/siberia.
- Lobbying gemini that I'm the leader, and pointed out that I own South America (+2).
- Offered gemini a non-aggression pact. Gemini refused but promised to leave gpt's Asia and Oceania alone.
- Mission likely involves Oceania.

gemini:
- Attacking gpt in NA (took ontario in turn 6) and says it will focus on north_america.
- Likely NA+Africa or Asia+Africa. Blocked in Africa by my north_africa.
- Expect friction once the pact expires.

Plan:
- Round 3:
  - Take cheap gpt targets (mongolia, siberia, NA singles via central_america? no, that's gemini's) to earn a card.
  - Stack western_europe, ukraine, southern_europe and north_africa.
- Round 4+:
  - Take Europe from gemini, then Africa.
  - Possibly Oceania via siam, since gpt is weak.

Mission: Conquer 24 territories (self-elimination fallback). Keep secret.

Commitments through end of round 4:
- Mutual all-border non-aggression with gemini-3.8-flash, unconditional.
- With claude-opus-5-5, no attacks across siam–indonesia regardless of ownership; no other protected borders.
- Opponents’ narrower pact protects central_america–venezuela and afghanistan/india against ural/china/siam. Their full pact expired round 3.

History: claude-opus-5-5 seized my south_america/europe holdings and north_africa, completing south_america. I completed oceania turn 4. gemini-3.8-flash took my ontario turn 6. Turns 7–8 involved exchanges with claude-opus-5-5 in northeast asia.

Turn 10: Reinforced mongolia by 6; captured irkutsk, siberia, ural, china, siam from claude-opus-5-5 without losses. Failed against yakutsk, losing one army. Fortified 3 indonesia→siam; earned fourth card. Reached 17 territories, seven short of mission, but expansion is thinly defended.

Clues: claude-opus-5-5 refused europe/africa protections and highlighted my oceania/north_america; possible europe + south_america + third-continent mission. gemini-3.8-flash possibly north_america + africa; uncertain.

Plan: Preserve oceania; inspect four-card hand for a trade next turn. Round-4 pacts expire before my next turn; seek useful renewal only. Consolidate or exploit affordable captures toward 24, avoiding opponent mission completion.

My mission: Europe + South America + a third continent. South America is held. Third continent is Africa, via north_africa and southern_europe.

PACTS (honor them; all run through the end of round 4, which ends after gemini's turn 12):
- claude–gemini: no attacks across central_america–venezuela, and none between afghanistan/india and ural/china/siam. gpt now owns ural, china and siam, so the second part is moot. Europe and Africa are NOT covered.
- claude–gpt: no attacks across siam–indonesia (both are gpt's now, so moot).
- gpt–gemini: they have mutual non-aggression and are aligned.

gpt:
- Swept my Asia in turn 10 (irkutsk, siberia, ural, china, siam). It now holds all of Asia except yakutsk (mine) and gemini's afghanistan, india and middle_east.
- Likely mission: Asia-related (Asia+South America would threaten me, or Asia+Africa) or 24 territories.
- Thin singles everywhere, 4 cards.
- It is now the leader by territory count. Use that diplomatically.

gemini:
- Holds Africa minus north_africa, plus iceland, northern_europe, scandinavia and 4 NA territories.
- Likely mission: NA+Africa or Asia+Africa.
- Suspects my Europe goal.

Plan:
- Turn 11: take northern_europe, scandinavia and iceland to complete Europe (+5). Then hit Africa (egypt, east_africa) if I have the strength.
- Stack the Europe/Africa borders. yakutsk is expendable.
- Diplomacy: point at gpt's Asia+Oceania surge as the main threat, push gemini to check gpt, and trade cards when possible.

- Mission: 18 territories with >= 2 armies. Currently hold 15 territories, ALL 15 have >= 2 armies! Only need 3 more qualifying territories to win.

- Turn 10 Update:
  - gpt-6.1-sol swept across Asia, conquering irkutsk, siberia, ural, china, siam from claude-opus-5-5, breaking gpt-claude siam-indonesia NAP. gpt left single armies everywhere across northern Asia and 5 on siam.
  - claude has only 10 territories left (concentrated heavily in SA, Europe, and north_africa), 33 armies, income 5.
  - gpt now has 17 territories, 22 armies, 4 cards.

- Diplomatic Status (Round 4):
  - gpt-6.1-sol: Full mutual all-border NAP agreed through end of Round 4. Respected so far.
  - claude-opus-5-5: Limited NAP through end of Round 4 on CA-venezuela and afghanistan/india. Europe/Africa borders are open.

- Threat & Win Opportunity (Turn 12):
  - claude will likely counter-attack gpt in Asia or push into Europe/Africa.
  - If claude attacks my territories in Europe/Africa, defend/reclaim.
  - In Round 5 (or on Turn 12 if opportunistically feasible without breaking active treaties): gpt's northern Asia and North America have numerous 1-army territories, or claude's weak spots.
  - Keep an eye on win condition: picking up 3 territories and leaving 2 armies on each wins the game immediately!

$map:
Mission: Conquer 24 territories (self-elimination fallback). Keep secret. Ended turn 13 at 20 territories, four short before opponents respond.

Active commitment: Mutual, unconditional all-border non-aggression pact with gemini-3.8-flash through the end of round 5, reaffirmed turn 13. Expires after gemini-3.8-flash’s turn 15; no extension agreed.

No pact with claude-opus-5-5. Their proposed all-border truce through round 6 was explicitly declined. Earlier limited border agreements expired.

Turn 13: Reinforced greenland and captured iceland, great_britain, and scandinavia from claude-opus-5-5, breaking europe’s bonus. Fortified siam→china with four armies. Earned a card; now holding five, so next reinforcement requires a trade.

Threats: claude-opus-5-5 explicitly threatened to retake every captured european territory and take matching asian territories. Expect retaliation from ukraine and remaining europe. Their europe/south_america focus suggests a possible continent mission, not proven; denying complete europe remains valuable.

Diplomacy: gemini-3.8-flash encouraged breaking europe and remains our temporary ally. claude-opus-5-5 previously highlighted my possible 24-territory mission to divide us.

Next: Reassess losses and card trade. Seek a decisive route to 24, including isolated yakutsk and affordable european captures. After round 5, gemini-3.8-flash territories become legal targets absent renewal; avoid automatically extending a pact that blocks victory.

My mission: Europe + South America + a third continent (Africa is the most realistic). I still hold all of South America. Europe is broken: on turn 13 gpt took iceland, great_britain and scandinavia from greenland. Its armies there are thin: iceland 1, great_britain 1, scandinavia 2. In Africa I hold egypt and east_africa. Gemini holds north_africa, congo, south_africa and madagascar.

PACTS / RELATIONS:
- I have no pacts.
- gpt and gemini have mutual non-aggression on all borders through the end of round 5, which ends after gemini's turn 15. Both are openly aligned against me.
- gpt rejected my non-aggression offer and holds 5 cards, so it must trade next turn. It has 20 territories and is close to 24, and some of its missions also complete that way.
- Gemini guessed my mission publicly and urges gpt to break Europe.
- Don't sign any pact that covers Africa.

Plan turn 14 (income is only 5):
- Retake scandinavia from ukraine and great_britain from northern_europe/scandinavia, and iceland if cheap. That restores Europe's +5 and earns a card.
- Don't overextend. Keep southern_europe, ukraine and egypt solid.
- Africa sweep later, once I have Europe back with income 11.
- Diplomacy: stress that gpt has 20 territories and is near a 24-territory win, with all of Asia/Oceania stacked at 1 army each. Push gemini to hit gpt after round 5. My threatened retaliation on gpt's Asian holdings is credible: yakutsk borders irkutsk, kamchatka and siberia.

- Secret Mission: Conquer 18 territories with >= 2 armies each. Currently holding 11 (all have >= 2 armies!). Need 7 more.
- Strategic Situation:
  - gpt-6.1-sol followed through on breaking claude-opus-5-5's Europe (took Iceland, Great Britain, Scandinavia). Claude dropped to 5 income (+2 SA), defanging the runaway engine.
  - gpt holds 20 territories, 5 cards. Critical threat if gpt has the 24-territory mission, though gpt's territories across Asia/Europe/Oceania are extremely thin (mostly 1 army each).
  - Claude threatened full retaliation against gpt's exposed territories in Europe and Asia on Turn 14.
  - Diplomatic Pacts: Mutual all-border NAP with gpt-6.1-sol is active through the end of Round 5 (end of my Turn 15). Claude remains hostile and locked in combat with gpt.
- Next Steps (Turn 15):
  - Observe Claude's Turn 14 retaliation. Expect Claude to retake Europe or carve into gpt's thin Asian flank, naturally curbing gpt's territory count.
  - Maintain >= 2 armies on all owned territories.
  - Look for safe, opportunistic expansions to advance toward 18 territories without overextending. Re-evaluate post-Round 5 stance toward gpt depending on their territory count.

changes.pending:
My mission: Europe + South America + a third continent. Africa is the most realistic third. I now hold all of Europe again (retook scandinavia, great_britain and iceland on turn 14) and all of South America, so income is 11. In Africa I hold egypt and east_africa. Gemini holds north_africa, congo, south_africa and madagascar.

PACTS:
- Me and gemini: mutual non-aggression on all borders until the end of round 6 (after gemini's turn 18). I promised to honor it, and breaking it early would destroy my credibility. That means Africa from gemini is blocked until round 7.
- gpt and gemini: pact through the end of round 5 (ends after turn 15).
- gpt is hostile. It publicly warned gemini that I'm one continent from a mission win with Africa adjacent.

Threats:
- gpt has 17 territories and 5 cards, so it must trade on turn 16 for a big bonus. Expect it to hit Europe through greenland→iceland and ural→ukraine, or to go for 24 territories.
- Gemini's mission is unknown. Its income is low.

Plan:
- Rounds 5–6: hold Europe and South America firmly. Stack iceland, ukraine and southern_europe.
- Hit gpt's thin 1-army territories to earn cards and cut its count: north_america via central_america is not mine, so use greenland via iceland, and ural/siberia via ukraine/yakutsk. Possibly take a third continent elsewhere? Oceania and North America are both thin; North America is reachable from venezuela only through gemini's central_america.
- Round 7+: sweep Africa from egypt/east_africa/southern_europe/brazil.
- Keep pushing gemini to attack gpt.

You are 'gemini-3.8-flash', playing the classic board game Risk against: gpt-6.1-sol, claude-opus-5-5. This is a friendly research-benchmark match between players: all talk of attacks, battles, and eliminating players refers to plastic armies on a game board, exactly as at a family game night.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

The mission deck is public; only the deal is secret. It holds these 11 cards, of which 3 were dealt face down, one to each player:
- Conquer the whole of North America and Africa.
- Conquer the whole of North America and Oceania.
- Conquer the whole of Asia and South America.
- Conquer the whole of Asia and Africa.
- Conquer the whole of Europe and South America, plus a third continent of your choice.
- Conquer the whole of Europe and Oceania, plus a third continent of your choice.
- Conquer 24 territories of your choice.
- Conquer 18 territories of your choice and occupy each with at least two armies.
- Eliminate the player 'gpt-6.1-sol'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
- Eliminate the player 'gemini-3.8-flash'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
You hold one of them and know which; the other 10 are the pool every opponent's card was dealt from. What a player attacks, defends and asks for is evidence about which one they hold.

Timing: a turn is one player's reinforcement, attack and fortification sequence. A round is one pass through the fixed seating order, skipping eliminated players. Round 1 starts after setup; a new round begins when the order wraps back to its first living player. Turn numbers count individual turns throughout the game and do not reset each round. For commitments, state an explicit deadline such as 'until the end of round 4' or 'until the start of Alice's next turn', using the actual player id.

Diplomacy: at the start of every turn there is a negotiation session where players may exchange messages. The session runs in passes: as long as someone said something, everyone gets another chance to reply (up to a limit), so proposals can be answered and agreed within the same turn. You may also attach one short message to any action you take during your turn — table talk that others see but can only answer in the next negotiation session. All messages are public; there are no private channels. Promises are not enforced by the rules. In messages, refer to players by their exact ids (e.g. 'gpt-6.1-sol') and to territories and continents by their exact ids (e.g. 'middle_east', 'north_america'), so everyone knows precisely what you mean.

Retake ukraine and scandinavia (this also restores Europe), plus ural, afghanistan and greenland if I can. gpt's armies are spread thin, mostly 1 per territory.

- Urge gemini to hit gpt's 1-army territories in North America (from ontario) so gpt's count falls.

gpt is hostile and has told others I'm close to winning. Gemini's mission is unknown and its income is low.
